hints: Convert all words to lowercase so comparison is case-insensitive.
Split the sentence by single spaces and count occurrences of each word using a hash map or dictionary.
Sort the unique words using a custom comparator: primary sort by descending frequency, and secondary sort by lexicographical (alphabetical) order ascending.
Format each word and its frequency as word(count) and join them with single spaces.
title: Sort Words By Frequency Problem

constraints: 1 <= number of words in the sentence <= 1000
Words are separated by single spaces.
Comparison is case-insensitive; words differing only by case are treated as the same word.
Output words are written in lowercase.
content.inputFormat: Single line: JSON array of all arguments, e.g. [arg1, ...]. The single argument is the input sentence as a string.
content.outputFormat: Single line: JSON-serialised return value. Words are listed as word(frequency), separated by spaces.

sampleTestCases.input: ["the cat sat on the mat the cat sat"]
sampleTestCases.explanation: Count each word case-insensitively, sort by descending frequency, and use alphabetical order to break frequency ties.
Words with different capitalization are combined into one case-insensitive word before sorting.

content.problemStatement: Write a program that accepts a sentence as input and returns the words rearranged in descending order of their frequency of occurrence. If two words have the same frequency, arrange them alphabetically. The comparison should be case-insensitive. Words that differ only in letter case must be counted as the same word, and the returned words should be shown in lowercase.

solution.approach: Normalize each word to lowercase, count frequencies with a hash map, sort the unique words by descending frequency and then alphabetically, and format the result as word(frequency).

better.description: Let n be the number of words and u be the number of distinct words. Count frequencies in O(n), then sort the u distinct words by descending frequency and alphabetical tie-breaking.

optimal.description: Let n be the number of words and u be the number of distinct words. Count frequencies in O(n), then sort the u distinct words by descending frequency and alphabetical tie-breaking.

bruteForce.description: For each unique word, repeatedly scan or compare all unique words to determine frequency and ordering without using a frequency hash map.

followUps: How would you optimize the solution if you only needed the top k most frequent words instead of sorting all unique words?
How would you handle punctuation marks attached to words if the input were arbitrary natural text?
Can you adapt the algorithm to handle a continuous stream of incoming words in real time?
